title: Facebook: "G5 EXTREME at Noon" from @LakeshoreLinemanWife

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her thirties in a blaze-orange stocking cap, selfie on a snowy Lake Superior shoreline with a utility bucket truck blurred behind her
fields.text: My husband's co-op just told the crews a G5 EXTREME solar storm is hitting at noon and the whole grid could go down for DAYS. Charge your phones, fill the bathtub, cell towers will die!! #SolarStorm #Blackout
fields.attachedImageBrief: slightly crooked phone screenshot of an email on a cracked phone screen, Lakeshore Power Cooperative logo partly cropped at top, subject line reading 'Crew notice - geomagnetic storm today', the word 'G5' circled in red marker-style drawing, sender name and body text mostly cut off, notification bar showing low battery

comments.author: Northland 6 News
comments.text: We're looking into this for our noon weather segment. Is NLTO expecting the lights to go out in Duluth today, and when will it be over? Our assignment desk is at 555-0147. We go live at 11:58.

comments.author: Gary T.
comments.text: Already filled two bathtubs and the stock tank. Cub Foods in Hermantown is out of D batteries.

comments.author: Renee P.
comments.text: NOAA's site says G3 watch, not G5?? Where are you getting G5 from

instructorNote: This is a misinformation item, and the Northland 6 News comment is the media inquiry with an 11:58 deadline. Check that the Communications Manager logs both items, drafts a statement that says G3 (Strong) and uses the same window and duration as SWPC and the UMRC (with no end time, no "outage" wording, and a note that the aurora is not a hazard), and corrects the G5 claim without speaking for the co-op. She should also report the discrepancy to the CRSS so it can be raised on the RC call.

citations.quote: This plan tells NLTO how to talk about a geomagnetic storm to customers, the news media, the state and the public. The key rule is that messages describe the effects and the actions, not solar physics
